answer:
When crafting your report, it makes sense to focus on effectively presenting your chosen statistics in a clear and logical fashion. Keeping a structured approach will make it easier for others to follow your reasoning, and using charts or graphs can significantly enhance understanding. This also allows you to present your perspective significantly, making it hard for someone to refute without concrete evidence. 

As you put together the data, consider framing it a way that leads the reader to your conclusion, but also keep some room for counterpoints to demonstrate your thoroughness. If you can weave in real-world examples or relevant comparisons, that will further strengthen your position. Prioritize showing how your data supports the narrative you want to convey, and just worth noting, everyone involved will be more engaged if they feel like they understand the underlying reasoning you've put forward.
